statement: A function $f:\\mathbb{R}\\setminus\{0\}$ satisfies $f(x+1)=f(x)+1$ for all real $x$ and $f(1/x)=-f(x)$ for all $x\\neq0$. Given $f(1)=0$, show that $f(n)=n-1$ for every integer $n$, and find the value of $f(2/3)$.
solution: From $f(x+1)=f(x)+1$ and $f(1)=0$ we get by induction $f(n)=n-1$ for all positive integers $n$. Also $f(0)=f(-1+1)=f(-1)+1$, while $f(-1)=f(1/(-1))=-f(-1)$ gives $f(-1)=0$, so $f(0)=-1$; descending gives $f(n)=n-1$ for all integers. Now $f(3/2)=f(1/2+1)=f(1/2)+1=-f(2)+1=-1+1=0$. Then $f(2/3)=-f(3/2)=0$.
hints: Use f(x+1)=f(x)+1 repeatedly to get f(n) for integers.
Relate f(0) to f(-1) via the second equation.
Compute f(3/2) from f(1/2), then use f(1/x)=-f(x).
